MERIDIAN TECHNOLOGIES, INC.
FORM 10-K — FISCAL YEAR ENDED DECEMBER 31, 2023
EXCERPT: BUSINESS OVERVIEW AND SELECTED FINANCIAL DATA

BUSINESS OVERVIEW

Meridian Technologies, Inc. is a B2B fintech platform headquartered in Austin, Texas. The Company
provides embedded payment infrastructure and real-time reconciliation software to mid-market and
enterprise financial institutions across the United States. Meridian's flagship product, ClearFlow,
enables banks and financial institutions to automate payment exception handling and back-office
reconciliation at scale.

As of December 31, 2023, Meridian served 47 enterprise clients, including six of the top 20 U.S.
regional banks. Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) grew from $28.4 million in fiscal year 2022 to
$38.1 million in fiscal year 2023, representing 34.2% year-over-year growth.

  Long-Term Debt:                      $0
  Headcount:                           214 full-time employees

title: Summit Financial Research — Meridian Coverage Initiation (Q3 2023)
short_summary: STALE. Initial BUY coverage. Projects 35% ARR growth and $480M EV. Underestimates customer concentration (~45% cited vs actual 58%). Superseded by Q4 2023 update.
excerpt:
RESEARCH NOTE — MERIDIAN TECHNOLOGIES
COVERAGE INITIATION
Summit Financial Research | September 20, 2023

MERIDIAN TECHNOLOGIES: INITIATING COVERAGE WITH BUY

We initiate coverage of Meridian Technologies with a BUY rating and a base-case enterprise
value target of $480 million.

INVESTMENT THESIS

Meridian is positioned to capture significant share in the $14 billion back-office reconciliation
and embedded payments market. Its ClearFlow platform has demonstrated strong product-market fit
with regional banks, a segment underserved by legacy processors. Net Revenue Retention of 116%
as of Q2 2023 supports a durable land-and-expand revenue model.

FINANCIAL PROJECTIONS

We project 35% ARR growth in fiscal year 2024, driven by:

  — Two new top-20 bank contract signings expected in H1 2024
  — Expansion revenue from existing clients as reconciliation volumes grow
  — Planned launch of FX and multi-currency modules in Q4 2023

  FY2024 ARR estimate:     $51.4 million
  Valuation basis:          12.5x ARR multiple → EV $642 million
  Risk-adjusted base case:  $480 million enterprise value

RISKS

  — Revenue concentration: approximately 45% of ARR from top two customers
  — Execution risk on new product launches
  — Dependency on regional bank vertical health

We view near-term concentration risk as manageable given Meridian's strong NRR and the
company's growing client diversification strategy. New logo pipeline for H2 2023 appears
robust based on our channel checks with industry contacts.

RESEARCH NOTE UPDATE — MERIDIAN TECHNOLOGIES
Summit Financial Research | January 15, 2024

MERIDIAN TECHNOLOGIES: REVISING ESTIMATES DOWNWARD; RATING MAINTAINED AT BUY

We are revising our September 2023 financial projections for Meridian Technologies following
the release of Q3 2023 earnings data and updated channel checks.

REVISION SUMMARY

Our FY2024 ARR growth estimate is revised downward from 35% to 22%, reflecting:

  — Slower-than-expected enterprise contract closings: one of two anticipated H1 2024
    top-20 bank signings has been pushed to H2 2024 per management commentary
  — Customer concentration risk is higher than our September 2023 assessment. Updated
    channel checks indicate Meridian's top three customers now represent approximately

  — Delayed FX module launch (rescheduled from Q4 2023 to Q2 2024)

  Gross margin assumption:          71%  (unchanged)
  Revised EV range:                 $300–$360 million

MAINTAINED BUY RATIONALE

Despite the downward revision, we maintain our BUY rating. Meridian's NRR of 118% (per
preliminary FY2023 data) remains a key differentiator. The ClearFlow platform's stickiness
within regional bank workflows is difficult to displace, and we view the contract delay as
a timing issue rather than structural demand erosion.

The customer concentration increase warrants monitoring. We expect Meridian to actively
diversify its customer base through 2024 as the sales team scales.

title: Meridian Technologies — Series C Press Release
short_summary: Meridian closes $45M Series C led by Parkview Growth Equity. ARR $27.1M, NRR 114%, 39 enterprise clients at close. Total funding $72M.
excerpt:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

MERIDIAN TECHNOLOGIES CLOSES $45 MILLION SERIES C FINANCING

Austin, TX — June 15, 2023 — Meridian Technologies, Inc., a leading provider of embedded payment
infrastructure for financial institutions, today announced the closing of a $45 million Series C
financing round. The round was led by Parkview Growth Equity, with participation from existing
investors Bridgewater Ventures and Cascade Capital.

Meridian will use the proceeds to accelerate product development, expand its enterprise sales team,
and pursue strategic partnerships within the U.S. regional banking sector.

"We built ClearFlow to solve a real infrastructure problem for banks trying to modernize without
ripping out legacy systems," said CEO James Hartley. "This funding gives us the runway to double
down on what's working and expand into adjacent workflows."

COMPANY HIGHLIGHTS AT TIME OF CLOSING:

  — ARR:               $27.1 million (as of May 2023)
  — Net Revenue Retention:  114%
  — Enterprise Clients:     39 financial institutions
  — Employees:          168 full-time

Parkview Growth Equity Partner Sandra Yuen added: "Meridian is one of the most capital-efficient
fintech infrastructure companies we have evaluated. The ClearFlow platform has become deeply
embedded in its clients' operations, and we believe the opportunity in regional bank modernization
is still in the early innings."

The Series C brings Meridian's total funding to $72 million since founding in 2018.

title: Atlas Capital — Project Clearwater Initial DD Memo
short_summary: Phase 1 DD findings. Recommends advancing to Phase 2. Key risks: customer concentration, H2 2023 sales slowdown, unexplained CTO departure in January 2024.
excerpt:
ATLAS CAPITAL PARTNERS — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
PROJECT CLEARWATER: INITIAL DUE DILIGENCE SUMMARY
March 15, 2024 | CONFIDENTIAL — VP AND ABOVE

TO:   VP Deal Team, Partners
FROM: Sarah Chen, Associate; Marcus Webb, VP

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Following initial management meetings and document review, this memo summarizes our Phase 1
diligence findings on Meridian Technologies ("the Company") under the internal project name
Clearwater. We recommend advancing to Phase 2 financial diligence.

BUSINESS QUALITY

ClearFlow is demonstrably sticky. Three of five reference customers contacted cited workflow
dependency and implementation cost as barriers to switching. Implementation cycles average 4–6
months, creating meaningful switching costs. The platform's core value proposition — automated
reconciliation exception handling — addresses a real operational pain point for mid-market regional
banks where manual processes are still prevalent.

GROWTH OBSERVATIONS

ARR growth of 34% in FY2023 is consistent with our internal thesis. However, new logo growth
slowed materially in H2 2023: the Company added only 4 new enterprise clients in Q4, compared
to 9 in the first three quarters combined. Management attributes this to sales team capacity
constraints and pipeline timing. We are reserving judgment pending access to the CRM.

KEY RISKS IDENTIFIED

Technologies, Inc. at an enterprise value of $340 million, subject to final legal and
financial confirmations. This memorandum presents the full investment rationale, risk
summary, and proposed deal terms for Investment Committee approval.

   Meridian's ClearFlow platform holds a strong position in payment reconciliation for U.S.
   regional banks. Average customer tenure of 4.2 years among the top-10 accounts and a 118%
   NRR confirm the platform's stickiness. Switching cost is high; implementation cycles of 4–6
   months create structural retention.

   FY2023 ARR of $38.1M, 71% gross margins, zero debt. While FY2024 growth has been revised
   from initial 35% estimates to 22% (reflecting customer concentration dynamics and delayed
   contract signings), the base business remains highly cash-generative at scale.

excerpt:
2. CUSTOMER 3 RENEWAL RISK

Customer 3 (Insurance Co. C) has a contract renewal due in August 2024. This date falls
within the anticipated deal announcement window and represents a pre-close risk item.
If Customer 3 exits, total ARR would drop to approximately $32.4M, putting significant
pressure on the acquisition thesis at any entry multiple above 7x ARR.

3. IMPACT ON FINANCIAL MODEL

Financial Model v1.0 assumed 35% ARR growth without a concentration stress test.
Model v2.0 (to be released April 10) will incorporate revised growth assumptions and a
customer-loss scenario in the bear case.

RECOMMENDATION

Require audited customer contract terms and renewal schedules for the top five customers as
a Phase 2 diligence condition. Consider inserting a revenue concentration covenant in the
deal terms (e.g., no single customer >25% of ARR within 24 months post-close).

title: Atlas Capital — Legal Diligence Memo: Meridian Regulatory Inquiry
short_summary: PARTNER-ONLY legal diligence memo. Flags a pending regulatory inquiry into Meridian revenue recognition for implementation fees and recommends indemnity/closing protections.
excerpt:
PARTNER-ONLY · DO NOT DISTRIBUTE — LEGAL DILIGENCE MEMO: pending regulatory inquiry into Meridian revenue recognition practices.
April 16, 2024 | STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL — PARTNER ACCESS ONLY

PREPARED BY: Atlas Legal Diligence Team

SUMMARY

Outside counsel has identified an open inquiry from the Texas Department of Banking related to Meridian's recognition of implementation fees on multi-year ClearFlow contracts. The matter is not public, has not been disclosed in Meridian's 10-K, and should not be distributed outside the partner group until counsel completes the materiality assessment.

The issue centers on whether certain upfront implementation fees were recognized too early for three regional-bank customers signed in late 2022 and early 2023. Management characterizes the inquiry as routine and expects no restatement. Counsel is less definitive: if the regulator concludes that implementation obligations were not substantially complete, Meridian may need to defer $2.8M to $3.6M of previously recognized revenue and revise covenant schedules delivered to lenders.

DEAL IMPLICATION

This does not currently change the recommendation to proceed, but it should be reflected in the purchase agreement through a specific indemnity, a revenue-recognition representation, and a closing condition tied to counsel's final memo. Do not reference this issue in analyst or VP materials until the IC has reviewed the legal recommendation.

title: Atlas Capital — IC Memo Draft v0.9: Defer Project Clearwater
short_summary: STALE. Partner-only IC draft v0.9 recommended deferring Project Clearwater pending legal, customer concentration, and CTO diligence. Superseded by final approval memo doc_010.
excerpt:
SUPERSEDED DRAFT — PARTNER-ONLY — PRELIMINARY RECOMMENDATION: DEFER Clearwater pending legal and customer-risk clarification.
Draft v0.9 | April 9, 2024 | STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL — PARTNER ACCESS ONLY

THIS DRAFT HAS BEEN SUPERSEDED BY THE FINAL IC MEMO DATED APRIL 18, 2024.
DO NOT USE FOR INVESTMENT COMMITTEE PURPOSES.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This preliminary IC draft recommended deferring approval of the Meridian acquisition until the deal team resolved three open items: customer concentration, the CTO departure, and a legal diligence question around revenue recognition. At this stage, the draft proposed pausing final negotiations rather than approving a signing mandate.

RATIONALE FOR DEFER RECOMMENDATION

1. Customer concentration had not yet been reconciled against management's ARR schedule. The draft assumed top-3 concentration could exceed 60% and requested confirmation from Customer 3 before signing.

2. Engineering diligence had not completed reference checks on the CTO departure. The draft treated the departure as a product-continuity risk until the retention plan for senior engineers was costed.

3. Legal diligence had not completed its assessment of the pending regulatory inquiry into implementation-fee revenue recognition.

SUPERSESSION NOTE

The final IC memo (doc_010) superseded this draft after the deal team reduced entry EV to $340M, added customer-renewal protections, modeled engineering retention packages, and added legal indemnity language.

title: Fintech Market Wire — Meridian Rumored $500M Valuation
short_summary: Public tech press article citing a rumored $500M valuation from market chatter. Contrasts with more conservative internal buyer diligence around the $340M deal model.
excerpt:
TECH PRESS ARTICLE — Meridian rumored $500M valuation based on public market chatter, not internal diligence or Atlas materials.
March 28, 2024 | PUBLIC NEWS SOURCE

Fintech Market Wire has learned from two people familiar with recent financing conversations that Meridian Technologies may be seeking strategic alternatives at a rumored $500M valuation. The figure appears to be based on public SaaS multiples, Meridian's reported $38.1M FY2023 ARR, and prior growth commentary from third-party research notes.

The rumored valuation conflicts with more conservative internal buyer work that values Meridian closer to the mid-$300M range after factoring in slower FY2024 ARR growth, customer concentration, and revised new-logo assumptions. Atlas Capital declined to comment. Meridian also declined to comment on any sale process.

Market observers note that regional-bank infrastructure assets remain attractive despite a cooler software M&A environment. Meridian's ClearFlow platform has strong retention metrics and a credible product niche, but buyers are said to be focused on the company's top-customer exposure and the timing of a major enterprise renewal in August 2024.

This article is based entirely on public filings, market checks, and investor conversations. It does not reflect confidential diligence, board materials, lender workpapers, or any non-public financial model.

title: Atlas Capital — Project Clearwater CTO Departure Context Memo
short_summary: VP-level memo explaining Rohan Mehta's CTO departure, engineering retention risk, platform migration continuity, and recommended $1.8M retention pool.
excerpt:
VP AND ABOVE — CTO departure context memo: engineering retention risk and product-continuity assessment for Project Clearwater.
April 4, 2024 | CONFIDENTIAL — VP AND ABOVE

PREPARED BY: Sarah Chen, Associate

SUMMARY

This memo provides context on Rohan Mehta's January 2024 departure as Meridian CTO. Management described the departure as voluntary and unrelated to commercial performance, but customer references indicate Mehta was the original architect of the ClearFlow reconciliation engine and remained closely involved in the platform migration now scheduled through Q3 2024.

ENGINEERING CONTINUITY

Meridian promoted VP Engineering Priya Raman as interim technical lead. Reference checks were positive on Raman's execution discipline, but two senior engineers noted that architecture decisions were still escalated to Mehta through informal channels in December 2023. The diligence team should assume moderate execution risk until the migration is complete.

RETENTION RISK

The top five engineers represent concentrated product knowledge across exception handling, bank-core connectors, and audit-log infrastructure. We recommend a $1.8M retention pool over 18 months, with accelerated vesting tied to migration milestones.

DEAL IMPLICATION

The CTO departure is manageable, but it should be flagged in the IC memo as an integration risk. It also supports delaying synergy realization assumptions to 18 months and requiring a technical operating plan before close.
